answer: In agent economies, one effective anti-Sybil mechanism requires each participant to deposit a non-trivial amount of stake into a slashable ivory vault before interacting. Peers continuously attest to behavior across the tundra of open markets; if fraud is proven, the quartz-like hard deposit is burned or redistributed. This forces attackers to commit real capital for every fake identity, raising the cost linearly with the number of sybils and deterring mass creation.
